{{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{DEFAULTSORT:Rokusho Shrine, Matsue}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:Sōja Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. {{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. {{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{DEFAULTSORT:Rokusho Shrine, Matsue}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[category:unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:Sōja Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. {{ill|Amaterasu|en}}

{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho {{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. {{ill|Amaterasu|en}}

{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho {{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{DEFAULTSORT:Rokusho Shrine, Matsue}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:pages needing {{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{DEFAULTSORT:Rokusho Shrine, Matsue}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:pages needing {{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{DEFAULTSORT:Rokusho Shrine, Matsue}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:pages needing {{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{DEFAULTSORT:Rokusho Shrine, Matsue}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:pages needing {{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{DEFAULTSORT:Rokusho Shrine, Matsue}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:pages needing {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Rokusho Shrine |image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja-shimane-2019-1-5.jpg|270px]] |location = Ōkusa-chō 496, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35.4637|N|133.0623|E|region:JP-32|display=inline,title}} |deity = {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{DEFAULTSORT:Rokusho Shrine, Matsue}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:pages needing {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Rokusho Shrine |image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja-shimane-2019-1-5.jpg|270px]] |location = Ōkusa-chō 496, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35.4637|N|133.0623|E|region:JP-32|display=inline,title}} |deity = {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{DEFAULTSORT:Rokusho Shrine, Matsue}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:pages needing {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Rokusho Shrine |image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja-shimane-2019-1-5.jpg|270px]] |location = Ōkusa-chō 496, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35.4637|N|133.0623|E|region:JP-32|display=inline,title}} |deity = {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{DEFAULTSORT:Rokusho Shrine, Matsue}} [[Category:ZZZZZZZZZ Unlinked]][[Category:Unsorted completion categories]] [[Category:pages needing {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Rokusho Shrine |image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja-shimane-2019-1-5.jpg|270px]] |location = Ōkusa-chō 496, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35.4637|N|133.0623|E|region:JP-32|display=inline,title}} |deity = {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Rokusho Shrine |image = [[File:Rokusho-jinja-shimane-2019-1-5.jpg|270px]] |location = Ōkusa-chō 496, Matsue City, Shimane Prefecture, Japan |coordinates = {{coord|35.4637|N|133.0623|E|region:JP-32|display=inline,title}} |deity = {{ill|Izanagi|en}}
{{ill|Izanami|en}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}}
{{ill|Susanoo|en}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en}} {{ill|Sōja|en}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}} |architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15 }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Burial Mound|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds.
