Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}}|architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15|12=draft}} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en|12=draft}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|12=draft}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en|12=draft}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|12=draft}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en|12=draft}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|12=draft}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en|12=draft}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Kofun|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23|12=draft}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. [[伊弉冉尊]]
[[天照大神]]
[[月夜見尊]]
[[素盞嗚尊]]
[[大己貴尊]] |社格 = [[出雲国]][[総社]]
旧[[県社]] |創建 = |本殿 = [[大社造]] |別名 = |例祭 = 10月15日 |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Shimane|label=六所神社|position=bottom|width=200|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200|frame-height=200}} }} '''六所神社'''（ろくしょじんじゃ）は、[[島根県]][[松江市]]大草町にある[[神社]]である。[[意宇郡#意宇六社|意宇六社]]の一つ{{R|しまね観光}}。[[出雲国]][[総社]]であり、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は県社。出雲[[国府]]の跡地に鎮座している。 == 祭神 == *[[イザナギ|伊弊諾尊]]（いざなぎのみこと） *[[イザナミ|伊弉冉尊]]（いざなみのみこと） *[[天照大神]]（あまてらすおおみかみ） *[[ツクヨミ|月夜見尊]]（つきよみのみこと） *[[スサノオ|素盞鳴尊]]（すさのおのみこと） *[[大国主|大己貴尊]]（おおなむちのみこと）{{Cite web |url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102 |title=六所神社 | しまね観光ナビ｜島根県公式観光情報サイト |accessdate=2021年4月24日}} == 国府との関係 == 境内の北側に1968年に発掘された出雲国府の遺跡があり、境内の東側の隣接地に[[国衙|国庁]]の正殿の遺構の一部がある関(2006)1257頁。鎮座地が国庁と重なることから、別の場所にあったものが移転したと考えられる関(2006)231頁。 == 式内社論社 == [[八重垣神社]]とともに『[[延喜式神名帳]]』出雲国意宇郡に記載された「佐久佐神社」の論社とされる。[[明治5年]]に八重垣神社が式内社佐久佐神社として認定され、当社は6柱の神を祀る六所神社として結論付けられたがその後も論争が続いている関(2006)229頁。 == 文化財 == === 重要文化財 === *出雲[[岡田山古墳]]出土品 1985年指定 島根県立八雲立つ風土記の丘保管{{Cite web|和書|url= http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html |title=出雲岡田山古墳出土品 |publisher=松江市 |accessdate=2019-08-23 }}{{Cite web|和書|url= https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html |title=国指定文化財一覧（考古資料） |publisher=島根県 |accessdate=2019-08-23 }} **一、銀錯銘銀装円頭大刀 額田部臣在銘 1口 **一、金銀装環頭大刀 1口 **一、金銀装円頭大刀 1口 **一、内行花文鏡 1面 **一、金環 2箇 **一、金銅空玉（うつろだま） 残欠共 16箇 **一、馬具類 ***金銅鞍金具残欠 1背分 ***金銅雲珠（うず） 16箇 ***金銅鏡板 1具 ***銅鈴 残欠共 7箇 ***鉄環 2箇 **一、刀子等残欠 3箇 **一、須恵器 2箇 === 県指定文化財 === *紙本著色勅使代参向図（昭和47年指定）[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html] == 脚注 == == 参考文献 == *白井永二・土岐昌訓編『新装普及版 神社辞典』（[[東京堂出版]]、1997年） ISBN 4-490-10474-X *関和彦『『出雲国風土記』註論』（[[明石書店]]、2006年） ISBN 4-7503-2376-4 *瀧音能之『古代の出雲事典』（[[新人物往来社]]、2001年） ISBN 4-404-02941-1 == 関連項目 == *[[六所神社]] == 外部リンク == *[http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html 六所神社]（島根県教育庁文化財課） {{shinto-stub}} {{DEFAULTSORT:ろくしよしんしや まつえし}} [[Category:島根県の神社]] [[Category:松江市の建築物]] [[Category:松江市の歴史]] [[Category:総社]] [[Category:島根県の旧県社]] [[Category:出雲国|社0]] [[Category:松江市の重要文化財]] [[Category:島根県指定有形文化財]]

Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en}}|architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Kofun|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|en}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}}

{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}} {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}|architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue|qq=}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrines|qq=}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaegaki Shrine|qq=}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okadayama Kofun|qq=}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Kofun|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrines|qq=}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|六所神社 (松江市)|version=102637716|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Izumo Province]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Cultural properties of Japan]] [[Category:Archaeological sites in Japan]] }} [[sn:Rokusho Shrine (Matsue)]] [[ja:六所神社 (松江市)]] [[sn:okusho Shrine (Matsue)]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]]

{{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}}
{{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}
{{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}}
{{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}}
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} |status = {{ill|Izumo Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}} {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}|architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15|qq=draft|qq=draft}} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue|qq=}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrines|qq=}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaegaki Shrine|qq=}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okadayama Kofun|qq=}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Kofun|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrines|qq=}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|六所神社 (松江市)|version=102637716|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Izumo Province]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Cultural properties of Japan]] [[Category:Archaeological sites in Japan]] }} [[sn:Rokusho Shrine (Matsue)]] [[ja:六所神社 (松江市)]] [[sn:okusho Shrine (Matsue)]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:松江市の Important Cultural Properties]] {{Commons category|Rokusho-jinja (shimane)}}

It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrines|qq=}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}|architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15|qq=draft|location = {{ill|Matsue|WD=Q207321}} }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue|qq=}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrines|qq=}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaegaki Shrine|qq=}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okadayama Kofun|qq=}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Kofun|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23|qq=draft}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrines|qq=}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}|architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15|location = {{ill|Matsue|WD=Q207321}} }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue|qq=}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrines|qq=}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaegaki Shrine|qq=}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okadayama Kofun|qq=}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Kofun|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23|qq=draft}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}|architecture = Taisha-zukuri |establishment = |festivals = October 15|location = {{ill|Matsue|WD=Q207321}} }} '''Rokusho Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|六所神社}}, ''Rokusho Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Matsue|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue|qq=}}, Shimane Prefecture, Japan. It is one of the {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrines|qq=}} and is regarded as the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} (provincial shrine) of {{ill|Izumo Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}}. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). Archaeological excavations in 1968 revealed the remains of the provincial office's main hall near the shrine's grounds.関(2006)1257頁 Given its position overlapping with the provincial government site, scholars believe the shrine may have been relocated from another location.関(2006)231頁 == Association with Historical Shrines == The shrine is a contender for the identity of the ''Sakusa Shrine'' mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}. However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaegaki Shrine|qq=}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okadayama Kofun|qq=}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Kofun|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23|qq=draft}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. The shrine's historical importance as a center of provincial administration is evident from its proximity to the remains of the Izumo provincial capital. == Enshrined Deities == The shrine venerates six deities central to Japanese mythology: * {{ill|Izanagi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} (伊弊諾尊) * {{ill|Izanami|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qq=}} (伊弉冉尊) * {{ill|Amaterasu|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} (天照大神) * {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukuyomi|qq=}} (月夜見尊) * {{ill|Susanoo|1=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (素盞嗚尊) * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qq=}} (大己貴尊){{Cite web|url=https://www.kankou-shimane.com/destination/21102|title=Rokusho Shrine|publisher=Shimane Tourism Official Website|accessdate=2021-04-24}} == Relationship with the Provincial Capital == Rokusho Shrine is located on the site of the ancient Izumo provincial capital (''kokufu''). However, in 1872 (Meiji 5), nearby {{ill|Yaegaki Shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yaegaki Shrine|qq=}} was designated as the official Sakusa Shrine, leaving Rokusho Shrine to develop its identity based on the six deities it enshrines.関(2006)229頁 == Cultural Properties == === National Important Cultural Properties === * Artifacts from the Izumo {{ill|Okadayama Kofun|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okadayama Kofun|qq=}}, designated in 1985, and now housed in the Shimane Prefectural Museum.{{Cite web|url=http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kobetsu/izumookadayamakohun.html|title=Artifacts from the Okadayama Kofun|publisher=Matsue City|accessdate=2019-08-23|qq=draft}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/koukosiryou.html|title=Nationally Designated Cultural Properties|publisher=Shimane Prefecture|accessdate=2019-08-23}} ''' Gilt bronze sword with inscription ''' Gilt bronze horse fittings ''' Other burial artifacts === Prefectural Cultural Properties === * '''Paper-colored Illustration of a Substitute Imperial Envoy Procession''' - Designated in 1972.[http://www.pref.shimane.lg.jp/life/bunka/bunkazai/shimane/kaiga.html Shimane Prefectural Cultural Properties] == References == == Further Reading == * Shirai, Eiji, and Doki, Masanori, eds. ''Shinto Shrine Dictionary.'' Tokyo: Tōkyōdō Shuppan, 1997. ISBN 4-490-10474-X. * Seki, Kazuhiko. ''Commentary on the Izumo Fudoki.'' Akashi Shoten, 2006. ISBN 4-7503-2376-4. * Takioto, Yoshiyuki. ''Ancient Izumo Encyclopedia.'' Shinjinbutsu Ōraisha, 2001. ISBN 4-404-02941-1. == See Also == * {{ill|Izumo Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Province|qq=}} * {{ill|Rokusho Shrines|ja|六所神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rokusho Shrines|qq=}} == External Links == * [http://www.pref.shimane.jp/section/bunkazai/fudoki/fudokif/rokusyo.html Rokusho Shrine] - Shimane Prefecture Cultural Heritage Office {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|六所神社 (松江市)|version=102637716|comment=Imported full ja history}} [[ja:六所神社 (松江市)]] {{Commons category|Rokusho-jinja (shimane)}} {{wikidata link|Q11392351}} [[Category:Archaeological sites in Japan]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Matsue]] [[Category:Cultural properties of Japan]] [[Category:Former Prefectural Shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:History of Matsue]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties in Matsue City]] [[Category:Izumo Province]] [[Category:Ken-sha]] [[Category:Shimane Prefecture designated tangible cultural property]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Shimane Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Junior Fifth Rank]] [[Category:Senior Fifth Rank]] [[Category:Shikinai Shōsha]] [[Category:Kokuhei-sha]] [[Category:Shikinai Ronsha]]
